evidence.quote: The M23C6 precipitates play a significant role in the creep resistance of superalloys.
Binary M23N6 nitrides have a lot in common with binary carbides. They were created by replacing C atoms with N atoms in M23C6.
Cr92C24 is indisputably the most cohesive phase compared to the other binary and ternary carbides
Fe92C24 also has the lowest G/K making it the most soft and ductile among the carbides.
Among the binary carbides, W92C24 has the highest K, G, and E values thus is the least compressible and the most rigid and stiff carbide.
Cr46W46C24 has the highest TBOD (0.0602 e/Å3) suggesting a cohesive nature but still less so than the binary phase Cr92C24.
Fe46Mo46C24 is also seen to be less stable in comparison to Fe46Cr46C24 due to its TDOS features near EF.
Fe46Mo46C24 has the lowest TBOD (0.0456 e/Å3) due to both the lower BO of Fe-Fe bonds and the larger cell volume.

evidence.quote: The electronic structure results discussed earlier show that W92C24 is the most stable binary carbides in terms of lowest N(EF) and relatively large TBOD thus show a direct correlation between electronic structure and mechanical properties.
